metadata.title: AASLD Practice Guidance on Prevention, Diagnosis, and Treatment of Hepatocellular Carcinoma
metadata.organization: American Association for the Study of Liver Diseases (AASLD)

epidemiology.trends: HCC is the most rapidly increasing cause of cancer death in the United States
epidemiology.nafld_emergence: NAFLD is becoming a leading cause of HCC, particularly HCC arising in non-cirrhotic liver

risk_stratification.hbv: Annual HCC incidence 0.2-0.6% without cirrhosis, 2-8% with cirrhosis
risk_stratification.hcv: Annual HCC incidence 1-8% with cirrhosis; remains elevated after SVR
risk_stratification.nafld: Annual HCC incidence 0.5-2.6% in NAFLD-cirrhosis; 10-20% occur without cirrhosis
risk_stratification.alcohol: Annual HCC incidence 1-4% in alcohol-related cirrhosis

target_populations.cirrhosis: All patients with cirrhosis who would be candidates for HCC treatment
target_populations.hbv_without_cirrhosis: Selected HBV patients: Asian males greater than 40, Asian females greater than 50, Africans greater than 20, family history of HCC, high HBV DNA
target_populations.post_svr: Patients with HCV and advanced fibrosis (F3) or cirrhosis after SVR
target_populations.nafld: Consider in NAFLD-cirrhosis; no clear guidance for non-cirrhotic NAFLD

modality.primary: Ultrasound with or without AFP every 6 months
modality.meta_analysis: Surveillance improves early detection (OR 2.08), curative treatment receipt (OR 2.24), and survival (OR 1.90)

ultrasound_quality.visualization: LI-RADS US visualization score should be documented
ultrasound_quality.inadequate: US visualization score C (severely limited) in approximately 20% of patients
ultrasound_quality.alternative: Consider CT or MRI for patients with inadequate US visualization

afp.galad: GALAD score (sex, age, AFP-L3, AFP, DCP) improves detection but not widely available

modality.abbreviated_mri: Emerging alternative with higher sensitivity; cost-effectiveness being evaluated

exclusion.condition: Child-Pugh C cirrhosis not listed for liver transplantation
Significant comorbidities limiting life expectancy or treatment eligibility

surveillance.interval: 6 months based on tumor doubling time data

li_rads.recommendation: LI-RADS classification recommended for CT and MRI in patients at risk for HCC

major_features.feature: Threshold growth (greater than or equal to 50% in less than 6 months)

ceus.role: Alternative for characterization when CT/MRI inconclusive or contraindicated

biopsy.immunohistochemistry: HSP70, glypican-3, glutamine synthetase panel for early/well-differentiated HCC

biomarkers.afp: Not sufficient alone for diagnosis; useful as adjunct

bclc_2022.modification: PS 0-1 for BCLC 0, A, B; PS 0-2 for BCLC C

stages.stage: Single less than 2 cm, Child-Pugh A, PS 0-1
Single or up to 3 nodules up to 3 cm, Child-Pugh A-B, PS 0-1
Portal invasion and/or extrahepatic spread, Child-Pugh A-B, PS 0-2
Child-Pugh C or PS greater than 2

portal_hypertension.hvpg: Greater than or equal to 10 mmHg indicates clinically significant portal hypertension

extrahepatic_evaluation.bone_imaging: If symptomatic or elevated alkaline phosphatase

multidisciplinary.recommendation: All HCC patients should be discussed in a multidisciplinary tumor board
multidisciplinary.evidence: MDT care associated with improved survival (meta-analysis)

indication.liver_function: Child-Pugh A, no clinically significant portal hypertension
indication.non_cirrhotic: Treatment of choice for HCC in non-cirrhotic liver

techniques.laparoscopic: Preferred when feasible; reduced decompensation, shorter stay
techniques.pve: Portal vein embolization for insufficient FLR (expect 20-25% increase)
techniques.tare: Y90 radiation lobectomy as alternative to PVE with simultaneous tumor treatment

portal_hypertension.selected: Selected patients with mild PH may undergo small resections
portal_hypertension.laparoscopic: Laparoscopic approach may expand resection eligibility in PH

techniques.surveillance_post_resection: CT or MRI every 3-6 months, shorter intervals in first year
techniques.hcv_treatment: DAA treatment after resection for HCV-related HCC (3-6 month observation first)

adjuvant_therapy.storm_trial: Sorafenib showed no benefit (RFS 33.3 vs 33.7 months)

imbrave050.population: High-risk HCC after resection or ablation

neoadjuvant.trials: Ongoing studies of ICI-based neoadjuvant therapy (cabozantinib/nivolumab, nivolumab/ipilimumab)
neoadjuvant.preliminary: Early pathological responses observed; needs further validation

criteria.milan: Single up to 5 cm or 2-3 up to 3 cm each, no vascular invasion
criteria.ucsf: Single up to 6.5 cm or 2-3 with largest up to 4.5 cm, total diameter up to 8 cm
criteria.toronto: Extended criteria with more liberal tumor burden cutoffs
criteria.afp_integration: AFP-based models improve selection (AFP less than 1000 ng/mL required for exception)

us_allocation.meld_exception: Automatic MELD exception for T2 HCC meeting criteria after 6-month waiting period
us_allocation.nlrb: National Liver Review Board for cases outside standard criteria

bridging.indication: Expected wait time greater than 6 months
bridging.modalities: TACE, TARE, ablation, SBRT - no proven superiority of one modality

downstaging.ucsf_criteria: Up to 5 tumors, largest up to 4.5 cm, total diameter up to 8 cm
downstaging.observation: 3-6 month observation period to assess tumor biology
downstaging.outcomes: Similar post-LT outcomes to patients presenting within criteria

living_donor.indication: May extend access, particularly in regions with long wait times
living_donor.outcomes: Comparable or superior ITT outcomes to deceased donor

ici_bridging.caution: ICIs before transplant may increase rejection risk
ici_bridging.washout: Consider adequate washout period if ICI used pre-LT

post_transplant.surveillance: CT chest/abdomen every 6 months for 5 years minimum
post_transplant.retreat_score: Risk stratification based on explant pathology (0-5 score)
post_transplant.immunosuppression: mTOR inhibitors may reduce recurrence in high-risk patients (SiLVER trial)

ablation.indication: BCLC 0/A, tumors up to 3 cm, not surgical candidates

modalities.rfa: Standard; best for less than 3 cm
modalities.mwa: Superior for 3-5 cm; less heat-sink effect
modalities.pei: Reserved for tumors where thermal ablation contraindicated

combination.tace_plus_ablation: May improve outcomes for 3-5 cm tumors

ablation.surveillance: CT or MRI every 3-6 months post-ablation

sbrt.indication: Alternative when ablation not feasible; bridge to LT
sbrt.evidence: Proton beam vs RFA RCT showed comparable outcomes for recurrent HCC

radiotherapy.nrg_rtog_1112: SBRT followed by sorafenib vs sorafenib alone - results awaited

tace.indication: BCLC B intermediate stage; unsuitable for curative therapy

techniques.tae: Bland embolization - comparable efficacy in some trials

tace.outcomes: Median survival 26-40 months with optimal selection

retreatment.art_score: Predicts benefit of repeat TACE; score greater than 2.5 suggests transition to systemic
retreatment.refractoriness: Failure to respond after 2 sessions or stage progression

combination_systemic.negative_trials: TACE plus sorafenib, TACE plus brivanib - no OS benefit
combination_systemic.launch_trial: TACE plus lenvatinib for advanced HCC - positive in Chinese population

tare.indication: Alternative to TACE for BCLC B; segmental PVT; bridge to resection/LT
tare.dosimetry: Personalized dosimetry improves outcomes (DOSISPHERE-01: greater than 205 Gy)
tare.radiation_segmentectomy: Curative intent for small tumors (RASER study: 88% pathologic necrosis)

trials.sarah: TARE vs sorafenib: no OS difference (8.0 vs 9.9 months)
trials.sirvenib: TARE vs sorafenib: no OS difference (8.8 vs 10.0 months)
trials.trace: TARE vs DEB-TACE: no OS difference but improved TTP with TARE

atezolizumab_bevacizumab.indication: First-line for BCLC C or TACE-refractory, Child-Pugh A

requirements.egd: Upper endoscopy within 6 months; treat varices if needed

durvalumab_tremelimumab.regimen: STRIDE: Tremelimumab 300 mg single dose plus durvalumab 1500 mg, then durvalumab q4w

negative_trials.leap_002: Lenvatinib plus pembrolizumab vs lenvatinib - did not meet primary endpoint
negative_trials.cosmic_312: Cabozantinib plus atezolizumab vs sorafenib - did not meet OS endpoint

ramucirumab.indication: AFP greater than or equal to 400 ng/mL

child_pugh_b.data: Limited; sorafenib mOS 5.2 months in B7
child_pugh_b.ici_data: CheckMate 040 subset: 12% ORR, 7.6 months mOS in Child-Pugh B7-B8

post_transplant.recommendation: ICIs contraindicated due to high rejection risk
post_transplant.tkis: Sorafenib may be considered with limited efficacy data

guidance_statements.statement: Atezolizumab-bevacizumab or durvalumab-tremelimumab preferred first-line for advanced HCC with Child-Pugh A
Upper endoscopy required before atezolizumab-bevacizumab; avoid with high-risk varices
After ICI progression, second-line TKI (cabozantinib, regorafenib) or ramucirumab (if AFP elevated) recommended
ICIs should not be used in post-transplant patients due to rejection risk
Advance care planning should be discussed for patients with advanced HCC

nafld_hcc.prevalence: Growing proportion of HCC cases, often diagnosed at advanced stage
nafld_hcc.surveillance_challenge: No clear surveillance recommendations for non-cirrhotic NAFLD
nafld_hcc.treatment_response: Generally similar outcomes to viral HCC when matched by stage

portal_vein_tumor_thrombus.classification: Main portal vein vs branch involvement affects prognosis
portal_vein_tumor_thrombus.tare: TARE may be considered for segmental/lobar PVTT
portal_vein_tumor_thrombus.resection: Selected cases with branch PVTT may benefit from surgery

palliative_care.indication: BCLC D, declining performance status, patient preference

components.advance_care_planning: Should be initiated early in advanced disease
components.hospice: Consider for those not benefiting from active treatment

palliative_care.reference: AASLD Practice Guidance on Palliative Care for decompensated cirrhosis

response_assessment.systemic_therapy: RECIST v1.1 standard; mRECIST provides complementary information
